analysis:
The PR gates exact-cache planning on an artifact-preload state machine. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied files.

cache_planning.go (head, lines 52-87) adds a gate on preload readiness. cache_preload_selection.go commits the plan only after two PlanningState observations (lines 52-64). A rejection takes precedence and is re-checked at commit, and an initial rejection cannot be promoted to Plan. Missing acknowledgement or participation fails closed to an empty CachePlanResult.

NoteDemand (cache_planning.go line 75) happens only after authenticated, memoized planning and a Registry rejection check. It carries only the (model, aggregate hash, contract ID, catalog generation) tuple from the verified catalog, with no account, prompt or body data. This is consistent with T-041's concern about cross-tenant cache and timing oracles. Consumers (ADV-002) can influence preload residency only via admissible models, at most 128 tuples. Rotation is rate-limited (30s replacement interval, 30s minimum residence, 5m demand expiry).

catalog/state.go refactors Snapshot into snapshotLocked, which is lock-correct. verified_preload.go produces a coherent snapshot plus artifact list under one RLock, with cloned strings and no paths or errors. cachePreloadIdentity linearly scans the verified list on every request, which is a minor CPU cost bounded by the catalog size.

active_set.go is a pure, serialized policy with no IO, auth or request state. It rejects non-monotonic clocks, generation overflow, and stale leases (operation and key must match). A key change or Invalidate marks an in-flight lease as invalidated, which prevents ABA. A failure backoff of <=0 invalidates the set. I traced nil-map paths after Invalidate and found none.

Coverage limits: PreloadController, promptcontract.Provisioner, Registry.CachePlanRejection and PlanCacheRouteWithResult, cachemetrics.CacheModelLabel and the callers of CachePlanner are not supplied. I did not verify that CachePlanner.Registry is non-nil (it is not nil-checked at lines 48-51), that PlanningState is thread-safe, or that PreloadPlanning wraps Preloader as documented. The threat model should note preload-driven demand and rotation if it is later enabled in production. T-041 is the closest entry.
